body:
Hi Vibhor,

I’m a UofT student on co-op in London working on search, planning and simulation for biotech automation, mostly around failure and recovery in large systems. I’ve also done a fair bit with RL and MCTS.

I’ve been looking for places where that work could be useful on real physical systems, and Burro stood out because outdoor robots have to deal with changing surroundings without someone constantly stepping in when something goes wrong. That navigation and recovery problem is pretty close to what I’ve been working on.

I was wondering if there might be a project I could take ownership of alongside my current work. One thought was a simulation and evaluation harness around navigation recovery, testing things like blocked paths or uncertainty in the robot’s position, but I’d much rather work on whatever problem would actually be useful to the team.

I attached my resume for context; happy to jump on a quick call if there might be something worth exploring.

Best,
Andrew
traits: Current work leads to what Andrew wants to pursue
Exploratory project ownership without automatic small/paid/contract phrasing
current_instruction_overrides: Use London, UK for future letters.
Do not copy this motivation or project into unrelated companies.
Batch repetition is a reason to inspect underlying thought, not paraphrase biography.
attachment_rule: Verify the actual resume attachment before scheduling. This revised exemplar was not the Burro email previously sent.
